title:
Some stories
should not disappear.
desc: Fóscolo & Company Edições brings together historical research, essays and literary creation. Each publication calls for its own form: a sequence of texts, an image, the rhythm of a page.
text:
Manifesto  Some stories should not disappear.    We live surrounded by information.  
We produce texts, images, research, records and opinions at unprecedented speed.
It has never been easier to publish. It has never been harder to remain.
  
Every day, new content appears and disappears. Archives are forgotten. Research becomes inaccessible.
Experiences accumulated over decades leave few traces. Institutions change. People leave. Stories disperse.
  Not everything can be preserved.  But some things must be.  
 
Fóscolo & Company was born from the conviction that publishing remains one of the most powerful forms of permanence humanity has ever created.
 
  Publishing is more than producing books.  Publishing is recognizing value.  
It is affirming that a certain experience deserves to be recorded.
That a certain work of research deserves to be shared.
That a certain memory deserves to continue producing meaning beyond its immediate time.
  
We are interested in stories that help us understand the world.
In research that expands horizons.
In essays that sharpen perception.
In literary writing that gives form to experience.
In testimonies that preserve memory.
In archives that hold trajectories.
In questions that remain relevant even when answers change.
  We believe knowledge should not remain restricted.  We believe memory is a collective heritage.  We believe culture grows stronger when it circulates.  We believe good ideas deserve readers.  Why we publish  
To preserve.
 
To share.
 
To build bridges.
 
To expand dialogue.
 
To transform knowledge into legacy.
  Our choice  In a time shaped by speed, we choose permanence.  In a time shaped by excess, we choose care.  In a time shaped by forgetting, we choose memory.  This choice guides every project we develop.  
 
Because some stories should not disappear.
 
Because some ideas deserve to remain.

title: There is more than one way into this book.
desc: Our inaugural essay on research, fragments, poems and images in Notes on Care.
text: Inaugural essay · August 2026  There is more than one way into this book.    Maria Carolina Fóscolo Gomes  Some books begin with a thesis. Others begin with a story.  Notes on Care, Risk & Knowledge  begins with a question: what do we do when familiar forms of explanation can no longer contain experience?  Historical research offers archives, interviews, protocols, and institutional traces. It makes it possible to reconstruct decisions, understand conflicts, and observe knowledge moving under pressure. Yet not everything a crisis produces belongs to the language of proof. There are silences, hesitations, and gestures of care whose importance does not diminish because they resist reduction to a category.  A fragment is not what remains of an unfinished text. It is a way of preserving what would lose its force if compelled to appear whole.  The book therefore places different registers in proximity. The essay sustains the question; the poem changes the rhythm; photography restores thickness to space; the archive resists seamless memory. None illustrates the other. They remain beside one another, producing a reading that is not linear, but attentive.  To enter through yellow fever is to observe disputed protocols and expertise. To enter through Zika is to see risk traverse bodies, families, and public responsibility. To enter through a suspected Ebola case is to follow the practical intelligence that emerges when prepared answers no longer suffice.  There is no single way into this book because there is no single way of knowing. Reading may begin with an argument, a pause, or a detail. Care is not merely the application of a correct answer. Often, it is learning to pay attention before an answer exists. title: A book begins before its first sentence.
desc: An editorial choice in Todos ou nenhum? — Book I: beginning with a sheet of paper.
text: Inside the editorial process · September 2026  A book begins before its first sentence.  An editorial choice in Todos ou nenhum? — Book I: beginning with a sheet of paper.    Fóscolo & Company Edições  A sheet bends under its own weight. Joined to others, it becomes part of a structure: pages, stitching, glue, a spine. The prologue follows this transformation before the first poem.  The opening brings together the book we read and the object we hold. It directs attention to the gap that must open between two pages before a sentence becomes visible.  This relationship runs through the volume. Iron, glass, light and paper remain specific materials with their own behaviours and limits. Bringing them close to human experience also requires acknowledging where the comparison ends.  Engravings interrupt the verbal sequence. Colour pages change the field of attention before a longer prose piece. Form shapes the pace without needing to explain the text.  The prologue offers a way in. Holding an opening precedes reading; the relationships that follow belong to each reader. text:
Research · circulation  Questions still in motion.  Fóscolo & Company books grow from a wider field of research, writing and public history. This page presents questions, contexts and trajectories — not unpublished originals.     01   Three research fronts      01  Health and institutions  How do institutions learn when health crises exceed protocols, routines and ready-made categories?    02  Science and classification  How does a virus collected in the Amazon become comparable, nameable and recognisable across international scientific networks?    03  Environment and infrastructure  Where does the forest end when ecology, surveillance and public-health infrastructure begin producing evidence together?        02   In circulation      May 2026 · UCL Institute of the Americas   Zika, risk and medical knowledge  A presentation on how guidelines, risk and public responsibility were produced during Brazil’s Zika epidemic.     22–25 Oct 2026 · SHOT · Johns Hopkins   The Environments of Technology  An accepted session co-organised and commented by Maria Carolina Fóscolo on infrastructure, materiality, evidence and expertise.     31 Mar–3 Apr 2027 · ASEH · Richmond   Where Does the Forest End?  An accepted presentation on yellow fever, nonhuman sentinels and public-health infrastructure in Brazil.        From research to the reader   Notes on Care, Risk & Knowledge already turns part of these questions into a public reading form: historical research, fragments, poems and images placed side by side.  The site presents questions, contexts, methods and routes of circulation. Submitted articles, manuscripts and unpublished originals remain off the site. title: Publishing does not bring things to an end.
desc: What changes when a book no longer belongs only to the table where it was made?
text: Circulation · September 2026  Publishing does not bring things to an end.  What changes when a book no longer belongs only to the table where it was made?    Fóscolo & Company Edições  For a while, a book lives inside a small circuit: writing, selecting, cutting, revising, designing and printing. Almost everything can still be brought back to the table and changed.  Publication changes that scale. The book enters an envelope, passes through other hands, reaches a shelf the publisher does not know and meets experiences that were absent while it was being written. A secondary passage for the writer can become the centre of somebody else’s reading.  Circulation is therefore more than physical movement. A book circulates when it creates unforeseen relationships: an image meets a memory, an argument meets disagreement, a question reaches another field of experience.  For an independent publisher, this passage belongs to publication itself. Finishing a file or producing an object is not enough. Publishing also means creating the conditions for a work to leave the place where it began without controlling what happens next.  Publication, then, does not close the work. It closes only one stage of control. The rest begins when the book is read by someone who was not at the table. title: From where does this table look at the world?
desc: Belo Horizonte is more than the address in the colophon.
text:
Place of publication · September 2026  From where does this table look at the world?  Belo Horizonte is more than the address in the colophon.    Fóscolo & Company Edições  Every publisher works from somewhere. Even when a book deals with questions that cross countries, institutions and historical periods, what first appears important begins in very concrete relationships.  Fóscolo & Company is edited in Belo Horizonte. Archives, universities, libraries, movement through the city, Pampulha and conversations taking place here form part of the repertoire through which books are read and prepared.  This does not mean turning the city into compulsory scenery or publishing only about Minas Gerais. It means giving up the fiction of a neutral point of view. Editorial choices have a geography too.  Circulation moves in the opposite direction: a book can leave a place without remaining trapped by it. It may reach another city, institution or language and meet questions that did not exist at the table where it began.  Saying where the work is made does not reduce a publisher’s reach. It makes visible the point from which it chooses to look. title: Empty space is also an editorial decision.
desc: Margins, distance and pause also organise a reading.
text: Form · September 2026  Empty space is also an editorial decision.  Margins, distance and pause also organise a reading.    Fóscolo & Company Edições  A page is made of more than what it prints. Before reading a sentence, the eye encounters margins, distances, alignments, blocks and interruptions.  These intervals establish hierarchies. Bringing two elements close together can make them appear to belong to the same argument; separating them can create a pause or prevent an easy association.  White space is therefore not an absence of work. In a book combining research, poetry, photography or essayistic prose, it can be the difference between piling materials together and allowing each form to retain its own presence.  There is also a limit. Emptiness should not operate as prestige decoration or as a way of making little content appear more important. Form must answer to the rhythm and function of the page.  Editing also means deciding what will not occupy space. Sometimes the best intervention is to leave enough distance for a reader to perceive a relationship without being forced to understand it in only one way. title: The uncertainty is in the first sentence.
desc: A reading of the opening of Machado de Assis’s “Missa do Galo”.
text: Repertório Fóscolo 002 · literature  The uncertainty is in the first sentence.  A reading of the opening of Machado de Assis’s “Missa do Galo”.    Fóscolo & Company Edições  Nunca pude entender a conversação que tive com uma senhora, há muitos anos, contava eu dezessete, ela trinta.  Machado de Assis, “Missa do Galo”.  The first sentence does not promise to clarify a conversation. It begins with the impossibility of understanding it completely.  The narrator looks back on an old episode knowing more than he knew at seventeen, yet distance does not become certainty. Memory supplies details without automatically resolving their meaning.  The opening is a useful reminder that ambiguity is not the same thing as missing information. A text can offer many elements while preserving more than one possible relationship between them.  Reading the sentence again changes the weight of simple words: “never”, “understand”, “many years ago”. The time of memory enters the story before we even know what was said that night.  This is the kind of return Repertório Fóscolo tries to practise: choose a concrete detail, return to it, contextualise what can be said and keep visible the point at which interpretation remains open.
